items.title: Louis Cottrell, Jr. Interview, 1961-08-25
items.q: I'll tell you someone that reminds me a lot of him now is Josiah Frazier.

ctx.x: Anything about his style of playing that you can say that is... Well, say compared to the drummers now. Of course, a lot of people think the drummers today are too noisy and jump all over the place, you know. Did he... Is he very active or was he a rather quiet drummer? Or what did you say?

Well, he was active, I think, for the period of time. I'll tell you someone that reminds me a lot of him now is Josiah Frazier. Oh, yeah. Yeah, it was more on that type. You see, just about the way Frazier plays, that was most of my father's style of playing. The way Frazier plays now.

Yeah, I was noticing Saeed the other week, he seems to hit the bass drum on one and three. One and three. That's right. That's the two beat. That's what they call the two beat. The one and three. And then his snares seem to more accent the two and four.

items.title: Josiah "Cie" Frazier Interview
items.q: Dennis Harris on saxophone and clarinet, Louis Contrell on saxophone and tenor sax and clarinet.

ctx.x: I'll leave this over there on tip on that. All right. That's all right. You can't hear it. You're talking about Bebe originally. Yeah, you know. And Papa Celestan.

Well, that time he used to...that we had the original Tuxedo Band. And then we used the title of the Young Tuxedo Band. Now that outfit consists of Dwight Newman on piano, and we had trained over to Paul Bent on trombone, Dennis Harris on saxophone and clarinet, Louis Contrell on saxophone and tenor sax and clarinet. And the regular rhythm section consists of White Newman piano, Lawrence Morale banjo, Eddie Morale bass, and myself drums. That was the regular rhythm. Eight pieces out.
What kind of a drum set did you get in the beginning?

items.title: Josiah 'Cie' Frazier Interview, 1961-02-16
items.q: And then we made it, uh, our band, eight-piece band, and we put Lloyd Contrell.

ctx.x: And then we made it, uh, our band, eight-piece band, and we put Lloyd Contrell. And the president of the local, he was, he was the first band he ever played with.
